To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the expression of the HuD protein is increased in SCLC and in carcinoids compared with normal lung tissue; 2) the HuD protein expression correlates with the level of anti-Hu antibody titers in SCLC; 3) somatic mutations in HuD gene have been detected in 35% of the analyzed neuroendocrine lung cancer tissues; 4) the HuD gene mutations detected in neuroendocrine tumors were not found in normal lung tissue;

the nELAV genes are involved in the development and/or progression of neuroendocrine neoplastic lesions of the lung, and that the genetic alterations in nELAV genes can be detected in the lung tumor tissues.

1) the HuD gene is mutated in a significant percentage of neuroendocrine tumor tissues; 2) the HuD mutations are inactivating and 3) the HuD alterations may contribute to the pathogenesis of a subset of lung tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular characterization of the n-ELAV gene family and their involvement in neuroendocrine tumors.
the role of HuD in lung cancer and its possible use as a biomarker.
the role of HuD gene mutations in the development of lung neuroendocrine neoplastic lesions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the involvement of HuD gene alterations is not frequent in the pathogenesis/progression of neuroendocrine cancers, and that the presence of anti-Hu antibodies is more likely due to a cross-reaction of anti-Hu antibody with a different antigen, rather than with the HuD gene.
the HuD gene could be involved in a small subset of neuroendocine lung tumors, but further studies are needed to confirm these findings.
the HuD gene is not a major target of somatic mutations in human neuroendocrine tumors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HuD gene mutations are rare but not absent in neuroendocrine tumors.
HuD gene is mutated in a small subset of neuroendrocrine tumors, suggesting a possible role for HuD in the development of these tumors.

1) the presence of anti-Hu antibodies is not a marker for the presence of somatic mutations in HuD; 2) the presence of somatically mutated HuD is associated with a poor prognosis; and 3) the somatic mutations in nELAV genes are associated with a subset of neuro-endocrine lung tumors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nELAV genes are potential candidate genes in neuroendocrine tumorigenesis and that they could be involved in neuroendocrine differentiation in SCLC.
HuD is an important gene in the pathogenesis and progression of neuroendocrine cancers, especially small cell carcinomas.
nELAV genes may represent new targets in lung cancer therapy.
